options.text: It returns adjacent JSX without one root value

questions.explanation: Adjacent elements must be wrapped in a parent element or Fragment.

questions.prompt: Which JSX correctly renders a dynamic image alt value?
questions.explanation: Use curly braces to pass the JavaScript value of `label`, not the literal string `{label}`.

questions.prompt: Which are common JSX mistakes? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: JSX has DOM prop naming rules and requires tags to be closed. Expressions in braces are normal.

questions.prompt: What is the safer default for rendering user text like `comment.body`?
questions.explanation: React escapes rendered text by default, which helps prevent script injection.

questions.prompt: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` should be reserved for trusted or sanitized HTML because it bypasses React text escaping.
questions.explanation: Injecting raw HTML can create XSS risks unless the content is trusted or sanitized.
The `&&` expression returns `0`, and React can render the number. Prefer an explicit comparison.

questions.prompt: Which JSX snippets are valid ways to conditionally render UI? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An early `return null` before the main JSX

questions.explanation: Ternaries, logical AND, and early returns are valid. A raw `if` statement is not an expression inside JSX braces.

questions.prompt: Which prop spread use is easiest to reason about?

options.text: Spread known safe props intentionally, such as `<Button {...buttonProps} />`
Spread every object from an API directly onto a DOM element
Use spread to avoid knowing which props are accepted

questions.explanation: Prop spread is useful when the object is intentional and understood; blind spreading can leak unwanted attributes or behavior.
